classification.difficultyReason: Match supplied shape descriptions to five curves and project each visible prominent peak to the x-axis. Two attributes are combined, but the choices and explicit peak-placement instruction keep the task a direct application.

content.prompt: Match each description with one of the curves shown below

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph bank, upper row, left
spec.description: Graph A: unshaded curve with a left-positioned peak, steep left flank and long right tail. Arrowed axes, rotated vertical title and uppercase graph identifier. No ticks, numbers or grid.
spec.mathematics: One prominent peak; positively skewed. Drawing coordinates describe a qualitative silhouette and are not numerical data.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure. No mode marker or supplied matching answer.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph bank, upper row, right of A
spec.description: Graph B: two approximately equal-height peaks separated by a valley well above the baseline. Outer tails descend towards the axis. Arrowed axes and rotated vertical title; no ticks, numbers or grid.
spec.mathematics: Two prominent peaks and an approximately symmetrical overall outline.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure. Both mode markers and the matching answer are withheld.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph bank, lower row, left
spec.description: Graph C: five distinct peaks and four intervening valleys. The third peak is tallest; outer peak heights and spacings are unequal. The unshaded curve begins and ends near the baseline. Arrowed axes and rotated vertical title; no ticks, numbers or grid.
spec.mathematics: Five prominent peaks. The distribution is roughly balanced, without exact reflection symmetry.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure. All five mode-marker positions remain unlabelled.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph bank, lower row, middle
spec.description: Graph D: right-positioned peak, long shallow left tail and steep right descent. The rotated vertical title retains two lines: Number of people / at concert. Arrowed axes; no ticks, numbers or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure. No mode marker or supplied matching answer.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph bank, lower row, right
spec.description: Graph E: unshaded bell-shaped curve with a central rounded peak and approximately matching tails. Arrowed axes and rotated vertical title; no ticks, numbers or grid.
spec.mathematics: One central prominent peak; approximately symmetrical and bell-shaped. No named probability distribution or numerical parameters are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure. No mode marker or supplied matching answer.

answer.worked: Graph A has one peak and a long tail to the right.
Graph D has one peak and a long tail to the left.
Graph E has one central peak, a bell-shaped outline and approximately matching tails.
Graph B has two approximately equal-height peaks on either side of a central valley. Its overall outline is approximately symmetrical.
Graph C has five prominent peaks, with two smaller peaks on each side of the tallest central peak. Its outline is roughly balanced, but the unequal peak heights and spacings prevent exact symmetry.

children.label: f
children.prompt: For each graph above, place an M on the $x$-axis directly below each prominent peak to show its mode(s).

answer.short: A: 1 M; B: 2 Ms; C: 5 Ms; D: 1 M; E: 1 M. Place each M on the $x$-axis directly below a peak.
answer.worked: Count every prominent peak, even when the peak heights differ. Place an M on the $x$-axis directly below each peak: one for A, two for B, five for C, one for D and one for E. The completed graphs contain ten mode markers.

spec.description: Complete graph A with one answer-only M centred on the horizontal axis below the peak.
spec.mathematics: One mode marker at the horizontal projection of the single prominent peak.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer figure only. The white mask behind M preserves legibility where the letter meets the axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph B and part f

spec.mathematics: Two mode markers aligned with the two prominent peaks.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer figure only. White masks behind the letters are structural, not area shading.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 graph C and part f

spec.mathematics: All five unequal-height peaks receive mode markers under the approved prominent-peak convention.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer figure only. Five structural white masks keep the axis from crossing the M letterforms.
